newsitem.title: USA: Southern Peru Copper expansion on track.
newsitem.headline: Southern Peru Copper expansion on track.

text.p: Higher copper prices, stronger sales, and lower taxes boosted Southern Peru Copper's second quarter earnings by $14.4 million or 32 percent compared with the same quarter last year as the company's expansion program gets underway, SPCC said Thursday.
SPCC has nearly $420 million of cash and marketable securities, and an undrawn committed bank facility of $600 million, the company said.
"These funds are sufficient to assure the financing of the company's $1 billion expansion program which is proceeding on schedule," SPCC said.
Site construction at Cuajone began this month, and engineering work on the Ilo smelter expansion is also underway, SPCC said.

Southern Peru reported net earnings of $59.6 million or 74 cents per share for the second quarter. Sales of products were $226.2 million compared with $173.2 million in the second quarter of last year.
Copper mine production fell two percent in the second quarter to 170.1 million pounds, with ore grades at SPCC's two mines, Toquepala and Cuajone lower.
"However, improved throughput and better recoveries offset much of the effect of the lower grades," SPCC reported.

In the second quarter SPCC sold 184 million lbs of copper, up 14 percent from the same quarter last year, with much of the increase made possible by concentrates purchases from third parties to meet the company's smelter requirements.
Sales of copper mined by the company rose by four million lbs.

Earnings in the second quarter rose by some $4.5 million due to the Peru government earlier this year approving a reinvestment allowance for SPCC to expand the Cuajone mine, effectively lowering the company's tax rate.
ASARCO Inc has a 54.1 percent stake in SPCC, with Phelps Dodge holding a further 13.9 percent. Common shareholders own 17.8 percent.
